newsitem.title: USA: Clinton widens lead over Dole; Perot gains.
newsitem.headline: Clinton widens lead over Dole; Perot gains.

text.p: President Clinton widened his lead over challenger Bob Dole by more than two points while third-party candidate Ross Perot also gained sharply in the Reuters daily tracking poll released on Saturday.

Clinton led Dole by 46.7 percent to 33.6 percent in the poll conducted for Reuters by John Zogby Group International. Reform Party candidate Perot's support stood at 7.8 percent, a jump from 6 percent on Friday, and 10.1 percent of respondents remained undecided.

The tracking poll surveys approximately 900 likely voters over a three-day period, creating a new three-day rolling average each day. The margin of sampling error is plus or minus 3.3 percentage points.
Perot received a burst of national publicity with his rejection Thursday of an appeal by the Dole campaign to drop out of the race and a Washington speech savagely attacking Clinton.
The Clinton-Dole gap widened from 11 points Friday to 13.1 Saturday as Dole continued to maul Clinton's ethics in his campaign speeches while the president virtually ignored his rival.
Pollster Zogby said that Perot had had two good days in a row - gaining 2.5 points.
"Dole has been particularly hurt by the awkward overture to Perot," Zogby said.
"In effect he has lost momemtum to Perot. Should this trend continue, Perot might hit double digits at Dole's expense."
